narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic journey and determined that there’s a **37% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that the school has decided you should take extra courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning sign—your current path has some risks, but with support, you can still reach your goals.

The biggest reason for this recommendation is that the model noticed **you haven’t shown strong plans to pursue higher education**. Most students who pass their final year are already thinking ahead to university or further studies, but this isn’t a priority for you right now. When students don’t have that long-term focus, they sometimes put in less effort, which can make it harder to pass.

Another key factor is **why you chose this school**. You picked it mainly because of its reputation, not because of the specific course you’re taking. Many students who struggle the most are those who didn’t pick their school based on a genuine interest in their field—it can make their studies feel less meaningful, and that can affect their performance.

Finally, the model also considered **how many times you’ve failed classes before**. While you haven’t failed any yet, the fact that this is a concern for the model suggests that your current study habits or engagement might not be strong enough to guarantee success. Most students who pass don’t have past failures weighing on them.

The good news is that this isn’t a final verdict—it’s a chance to adjust your approach. Focus on setting clear goals for your future, like planning for higher education, even if it’s just exploring options. Also, think about whether this school is still the right fit for you. If you’re not passionate about your course, it might be worth talking to a counselor about alternatives. And since you haven’t struggled before, now is the time to step up your study habits—maybe by dedicating more time to your work or seeking extra support if needed. With these changes, you can turn this warning into a stepping stone for success.
